records.title: Drug Discovery, Development and Beyond: Careers and Controversies
records.header: PHRMSC 201 Drug Discovery, Development and Beyond: Careers and Controversies (3) NSc
records.text: PHRMSC 201 Drug Discovery, Development and Beyond: Careers and Controversies (3) NSc Introduces students to drug development from discovery to drug approval with an emphasis on careers and the scientific and ethical issues at each stage. Recommended for undergraduate health science majors and non-science majors. Recommended: basic high school knowledge of general chemistry and biology. Offered: jointly with PCEUT 201.

records.text: PHRMSC 312 The Science of Drugs (3) NSc Introduces students to medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutical sciences. Prerequisite: either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257; recommended: basic knowledge in general chemistry and organic chemistry. Offered: jointly with MEDCH 327; Sp.

records.title: Introduction to Health Economics
records.header: PHRMSC 330 Introduction to Health Economics (3) SSc
records.text: PHRMSC 330 Introduction to Health Economics (3) SSc Applies core microeconomic concepts to the study of health care markets and the U.S. health systems. Students use economic models and analytic tools to explore a wide range of topics such as health insurance design, provider incentives, pharmaceutical markets, and current health policy debates. Recommended: ECON 200. Offered: jointly with ECON 344/HEOR 340; A.

records.title: Principles of Pharmacology
records.text: PHRMSC 401 Principles of Pharmacology (2) NSc Covers fundamental mechanisms of therapeutic drug action in both health and disease. Key topics include how therapeutics interact with the body, routes of medicine administration, and the basics of major therapeutic classes. Prerequisite: either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257; recommended: one of the following: (1) BIOC 405 and BIOC 406; (2) BIOC 440; BIOC 441; and BIOC 442; (3) BIOL 355; (4) coursework in cell biology. Offered: jointly with PHARM 401; A.

records.title: Global Health Pharmacy: Medicines, Practice, and Policy
records.header: PHRMSC 431 Global Health Pharmacy: Medicines, Practice, and Policy (2)
records.text: PHRMSC 431 Global Health Pharmacy: Medicines, Practice, and Policy (2) Introduces the critical role of pharmaceuticals in addressing major diseases (such as HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis) affecting persons in resource-limited settings. Addresses the wide range of relevant issues, including burden of disease, human resource capacity, regulation, drug safety/pharmacovigilance, drug distribution, pharmacoeconomics, financing, intellectual property, and drug trade policies. Offered: W.

records.title: Introduction to Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
records.header: PHRMSC 432 Introduction to Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (2)
records.text: PHRMSC 432 Introduction to Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (2) Provides an introduction to economic evaluation and outcomes research related to pharmaceuticals and other healthcare technologies. Covers the methods of cost-effectiveness analysis and quality of life evaluation, and their use in real-world decision-making. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Application of Machine Learning in Health Economics and Outcomes Research
records.header: PHRMSC 433 Application of Machine Learning in Health Economics and Outcomes Research (3)
records.text: PHRMSC 433 Application of Machine Learning in Health Economics and Outcomes Research (3) Introduction to machine learning methods, focusing on understanding applied literature, gaining hands-on experience with basic analysis to address health outcomes, policy, and economics related questions, and communicating results to a general scientific audience. Provides overview of topics related to using machine learning for medical decision-making, including model evaluation, algorithmic bias, model shift, and simulation modeling. Prerequisite: one 300-level STAT course; recommended: advanced coursework in either statistics, biostatistics, or econometrics; and familiarity with multivariable statistical methods, including linear and logistic regression. Offered: jointly with HEOR 452; Sp.
records.recommendedPreparationText: advanced coursework in either statistics, biostatistics, or econometrics; and familiarity with multivariable statistical methods, including linear and logistic regression.

records.title: Introduction to Mass Spectrometry
records.header: PHRMSC 441 Introduction to Mass Spectrometry (2) NSc
records.text: PHRMSC 441 Introduction to Mass Spectrometry (2) NSc Covers the basics of modern ionization methods and mass analyzers; small molecule structure assignment, quantitative assay development by Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS) and metabolomics; quantitative discovery-based proteomics and validation methods; and peptide sequence determination, post-translational modification mapping, and protein structure determination methods. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; and BIOL 220. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Biotechnology and Biopharmaceuticals
records.text: PHRMSC 452 Biotechnology and Biopharmaceuticals (2) Current topics in pharmaceuticals and biotechnology focusing on transforming small molecules, proteins, and genes into therapeutic products. Includes new drug therapies, drug design, pharmacogenomics, molecular modeling, high throughput screen, production and stability considerations, and delivery systems of protein and gene therapeutics in relation to pharmacokinetic and therapeutic responses. Recommended: basic knowledge in biology and general chemistry. Offered: A.
